kpis.label: Europe & Canada added $90B+ in 2021-price terms in 2025 (~20% YoY, NATO update Jul 7); EU spend reached €392B (2.1% GDP), with Germany's 2026 budget at €117.2B (→€162B/3.2% GDP by 2029) and France's at €68.5B (2.25% GDP); 5 Allies now expected to hit the 3.5% core-defense guideline in 2026
Defense tech VC funding hit a new full-year record in barely five months (Crunchbase); megarounds from Anduril, Shield AI, Saronic and Helsing keep the pace climbing
Defense Autonomous Warfare Group request, part of a ~$75B unmanned/counter-drone package; CCA Increment 1 production already awarded in June to Anduril & General Atomics — Kratos was not selected

private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: Talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed a month later, as of Aug 17 — over 3x the $30.5B mark from just over a year ago and up from the $61B May 2026 round (Thrive Capital, a16z). One floated structure would commit investors now to a second, higher-priced raise within about a year if Anduril hits financial benchmarks. CEO has separately said it's "bad to IPO in the middle of a hype cycle," delaying listing plans amid concerns defense-tech valuations are overheated.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI
private_watchlist.note: No new financing news this period; still marked by the $2B Series G (Mar 26, 2026) co-led by Advent International and JPMorgan's Security & Resiliency Initiative, plus $500M in non-dilutive preferred equity from Blackstone. Hivemind autonomy software; V-BAT drones.

private_watchlist.name: Saronic
private_watchlist.note: No new financing news this period; still marked by the $1.75B Series D led by Kleiner Perkins (with Advent, Bessemer, a16z, Franklin Templeton). Plans to build 20+ autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027.

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: $1.8B round closed Jul 13, 2026 (JPMorgan, Lightspeed, Iconiq); demand exceeded allocation. AI software + strike drones, Europe's rearmament wave.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations already stretched
bear_case.description: The US Aerospace & Defense industry trades around 32-33x trailing earnings (CSIMarket) — well above its historical range. Palantir has already eased from a $207.52 52-week high to ~$174 despite raised guidance, and even Anduril's own CEO has warned publicly against IPO'ing "in the middle of a hype cycle" — a notable caution signal from an insider riding the sector's biggest private markup.

bear_case.title: Capital outrunning production capacity
bear_case.description: Defense tech VC funding topped $14.6B in barely five months of 2026, already a full-year record. Commentators have warned capital is moving faster than governments can convert new technology into recurring production orders — a mismatch that could leave late-stage private rounds overextended.

bear_case.title: Budget and trade politics
bear_case.description: FY27 requests aren't appropriations; NATO's 5%-of-GDP-by-2035 pledge is real money on paper but still depends on political follow-through year after year. The new Aug 13 tariff proclamation (up to 100% on imported drones) also raises input-cost and retaliation risk for primes with global supply chains, even as it favors pure-play US drone makers.

bear_case.title: Strong headline prints can still hide execution risk
bear_case.description: Rheinmetall's Q2 profit nearly doubled, yet the company cut FY26 revenue guidance days later on a naval-programme setback — proof that a strong topline doesn't guarantee a clean guide. Kratos remains excluded from the June CCA Increment 1 production award (Anduril and General Atomics won instead) despite this week's new contract wins. Red Cat's 527% revenue growth still came with a consensus miss and a widened net loss. AeroVironment separately still faces multiple unresolved securities-fraud class actions.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: The Aug 13 FY26 revenue guidance cut (to €13.7-14.2B, from up to €14.5B) after a naval-programme setback overshadows the strong Q2 profit and ATACMS MoU narrative; still directly accessible via European exchange access from the UK without a US wrapper, but conviction is lowered until the naval issue is resolved.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: The £5.9B Dreadnought contract (Aug 4) plus a £135M torpedo-maintenance deal and a $150M USS Boxer award show broad-based order momentum on top of the H1 guidance upgrade; still the most straightforward name for you to hold — UK-listed, no wrapper needed.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Raised FY26 guidance plus a new ~$12B/$2B-profit 7-year Lockheed framework for THAAD/PAC-3 motors and the Arsenal of Freedom GMLRS facility opening add real backlog; the missile-business IPO/spinoff slipping to 2027 is a minor timing wrinkle, not a thesis breaker. Also sits in the Space sleeve via its payload work — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Stock has eased to ~$174 (Aug 16) from its $207.52 52-week high but still trades at an extreme multiple against mid-90s% growth; waiting for a more durable pullback rather than chasing. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: Stock extended its run to ~$196 (Aug 11) and picked up a Piper Sandler Buy plus a structural tailwind from the Aug 13 tariff proclamation on imported drones; kept speculative given how far/fast it's run (~35% in two weeks) and unresolved securities litigation. Also in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: New Javelin Seeker (Army DEVCOM C5ISR) and a $156M DOE/NNSA counter-UAS IDIQ (Solar Shield) show real revenue outside the CCA program it lost in June; stock rebounded ~30% in a week to the mid-$60s against a $105.62 average analyst target — enough to move this off pure watch into a small speculative position. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: Q2 revenue +527% YoY but missed consensus by ~11% and GAAP EPS also missed; the tariff-driven share pop doesn't change that losses are still deep and dilution risk is unresolved.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Record Q2 revenue of $83.8M (~13x YoY) and FY26 guidance raised to $525-550M genuinely answer the prior sub-scale critique, but margin and profitability visibility aren't proven yet, so this moves up to watch rather than straight into a position.
